input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

This looks like a CRLF line-ending issue, not a column mismatch. `parseStatement` splits the file on `"\n"` only and never strips a trailing `\r`, so when a file uses Windows-style CRLF line endings (as a new export tool would produce), the last header column comes out as e.g. `"description\r"` instead of `"description"`. That fails the `REQUIRED_COLUMNS` check in `assertShape`, which is called with `index = 0` for the header — exactly matching the "row 1" error reporters are seeing, even though the visible column names are unchanged. Fix would be to strip a trailing `\r` from each line (or split on `/\r\n|\n/`) before parsing the header and rows.

input.title: Handle CRLF line endings in CSV parser
input.body:
File: src/ingest/parser.ts. parseStatement splits the uploaded text on "
" only, so files with Windows-style CRLF line endings (as produced by the new accounting export tool) leave a trailing "" on the last field of each line. For the header row this means the last column name (e.g. "description") no longer matches REQUIRED_COLUMNS, so assertShape's missingRequired check fails and throws "Malformed row" for row 1 every time. Fix by stripping a trailing "" from each line (or splitting on /
|
/) before further processing, so both Unix and Windows line endings parse correctly.
